details.description: A deposit, a reference, a month's notice and somewhere else to go - in a market where she is already at the bottom. The exit is priced out of reach, which is the condition being exploited.
details.energy_note: The door is unlocked and costs four thousand to walk through.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the boiler
details.description: Third week without hot water. 'I'll be honest, I've been stretched. Rent's due Friday, isn't it.' A pause. 'Unless we come to something.' He has not said anything. She will not be able to quote a sentence.
details.energy_note: Nothing said, and she understood it exactly.

issues.title: The uniform as the opportunity
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Can use or threaten force lawfully or otherwise
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable as abuse by a bystander
issues.recourse_note: No mechanism exists
issues.summary: Sexual misconduct by people whose authority makes refusal dangerous, against people whose circumstances make reporting impossible.

details.aspect: The recorded scale is a floor
details.description: US officers were charged with forcible rape 405 times between 2005 and 2013 - about 45 a year - with forcible fondling more common at 636 instances. Researchers note data on sexual assaults by police are almost nonexistent, so these are charges, not incidence.
details.energy_note: Four hundred and five charges, and no denominator.

details.aspect: It is described in the literature as extortion
details.description: Documented patterns include intimidating vulnerable people with lies and half-truths to obtain sexual activity in exchange for their freedom - the leverage being arrest rather than force.
details.energy_note: The threat is the paperwork, not the weapon.

details.aspect: The targets are chosen for their irreportability
details.description: Those most affected come from marginalised groups - women of colour, LGBTQ+ people, sex workers, and people vulnerable to threats of incarceration - selected because a complaint from them will not be believed.
details.energy_note: Picked for who nobody will believe.

details.aspect: It is second only to excessive force in reported misconduct
details.description: One study found an officer caught committing sexual abuse or sexualised misconduct at least every five days; another found sexual violence the second most reported category of misconduct.
details.energy_note: Every five days, in the cases that surfaced.

issues.title: Looked at
issues.power_abuse_note: Happens between equals too, but is transformed by power
issues.power_type_note: Controls reputation, belonging or standing in a group
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: No mechanism exists
issues.summary: Nothing is said and nothing is touched. The target is nonetheless certain, and has nothing whatsoever to report.

details.aspect: There is no incident
details.description: A duration of gaze, a route taken past a desk, a presence in a stockroom. Each is nothing. The pattern is unmistakable and consists entirely of nothings.
details.energy_note: A pattern made of things that did not happen.

details.aspect: Reporting requires describing looking
details.description: Any account sounds paranoid when written down, which the person doing it relies on and may well have tested before.
details.energy_note: Say it aloud and hear how it sounds.

details.aspect: The target reorganises around it
details.description: Different route to the printer, never last to leave, cardigan kept on the chair. Unpaid, continuous, and invisible to everyone including the people who would want to help.
details.energy_note: A set of rules she follows and has never told anyone.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the stockroom
details.description: He is always already in there. Every time. He is polite, he moves aside, he says something about the weather. On the eleventh occasion she starts going at lunch instead, and nothing has happened, and nothing will.
details.energy_note: Eleven times, and not one thing to report.

issues.title: Afterwards: what the institution does
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Acts as or is shielded by an organisation
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: The complaint is made, and the process becomes the second event - frequently the one the target describes as worse.

details.aspect: She is investigated too
details.description: Her performance, her attendance, her prior conduct and her motives all become material, because the process is framed as fact-finding between two accounts.
details.energy_note: Both of you are being looked into now.

details.aspect: Confidentiality runs one way
details.description: She is reminded of her obligations. He is not prevented from speaking to anybody, and does.
details.energy_note: She is bound to silence while he explains.

details.aspect: The outcome is unsubstantiated and both remain
details.description: No finding either way, no sanction, and a working arrangement that requires her to keep seeing him - which is generally when people leave.
details.energy_note: Nothing proven, nothing changed, and she resigns in March.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the informal resolution
details.description: 'We could do this formally. But formal means statements, and it means his side, and honestly it means everyone knowing.' The HR partner is kind and is not lying. 'Or I can have a quiet word with him.' The quiet word happens. He is told who complained.
details.energy_note: Offered the kind option, and it tells him her name.

issues.title: Coercive control
issues.power_abuse_note: Happens between equals too, but is transformed by power
issues.power_type_note: Controls reputation, belonging or standing in a group
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists and sometimes works
issues.summary: Stark's insight: the harm is a pattern of domination, not a series of assaults. Most of the individual acts are lawful, which is exactly why the old incident-based model could not see it.

details.aspect: The definition
details.description: A pattern of domination including strategies to isolate, exploit and regulate the everyday behaviour of the victim. Stark likened it to being taken hostage - entrapped in confusion, contradiction and fear.
details.energy_note: Not incidents. A condition of life.
details.notes: Stark, Coercive Control: How Men Entrap Women in Personal Life.

details.aspect: Individually lawful, collectively the offence
details.description: Rules about dress, spending, timekeeping and who may be seen - each of which, alone, is not abuse. Stark's point is that the combination constitutes it.
details.energy_note: Nothing on the list is a crime. The list is.

details.aspect: The law caught up partially and recently
details.description: Controlling or coercive behaviour became an offence in England and Wales under section 76 of the Serious Crime Act 2015, maximum five years. California incorporated coercive control into the domestic violence definition from January 2021.
details.energy_note: Illegal since 2015, in some places.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the receipts
details.description: He does not forbid anything. He asks about the £14 at the chemist, warmly, at dinner, in front of her sister. And about the £6 on Tuesday. He remembers all of them. She starts paying cash so there is nothing to ask about, and that is the whole mechanism.
details.energy_note: Never told not to. Just always asked about.

details.aspect: The exit is the most dangerous part and everyone asks why she stayed
details.description: Regulation intensifies at separation, the resources to leave have usually been removed first, and the question put to her afterwards is about her choices.
details.energy_note: Asked why she stayed, by people who removed the exits.

issues.title: Economic control
issues.power_abuse_note: Happens between equals too, but is transformed by power
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists and sometimes works
issues.summary: One of three recognised domains of economic abuse: restricting the partner's capacity to acquire, use or maintain money at all.

details.aspect: The recognised tactics
details.description: Controlling resources, denying necessities, tracking spending, withholding or hiding jointly earned money, lying about assets, refusing access to an account, changing passwords, hiding documents.
details.energy_note: Not poverty. Administration.

details.aspect: Documents as leverage
details.description: Withholding passports, ID, insurance papers or employment contracts makes it difficult to apply for jobs, register for courses or claim entitlements - the identity itself held as security.
details.energy_note: Her passport, in his drawer, for six years.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the joint account
details.description: 'It's easier if it all comes into mine, then I do the transfers.' It is easier. After four months the transfers arrive late. After a year she asks for the login and he is hurt that she does not trust him.
details.energy_note: Efficient, then late, then his feelings are the subject.

details.aspect: It is common and not widely recognised as abuse
details.description: Lifetime prevalence among ever-partnered women runs 11-15% in general populations and 76-99% among those seeking services for intimate partner violence.
details.energy_note: Three quarters and up, among those already seeking help.

issues.title: Employment sabotage
issues.power_abuse_note: Happens between equals too, but is transformed by power
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: The second domain: preventing the partner from getting or keeping work, which removes the money, the independence and the witnesses at once.

details.aspect: The documented tactics
details.description: Forbidding or interfering with work and study, harassing her at the workplace, contacting a supervisor to tell lies or disclose private information, obstructing other income such as child support or benefits.
details.energy_note: Calling her manager, and telling him things.

details.aspect: It works because employers act on it
details.description: Repeated calls, scenes at reception and disclosures to colleagues make her a problem at work regardless of who caused it, and she is the one who becomes unemployable.
details.energy_note: He causes the scenes and she loses the job.

details.aspect: It serves several purposes at once
details.description: It limits income, erodes self-esteem, isolates her socially and reinforces financial dependency - which is why it is a strategy rather than an outburst.
details.energy_note: One act, four results, all of them useful to him.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the interview morning
details.description: The interview is at ten. At nine he cannot find the car key and is very sorry. At nine-twenty he needs to talk about something important that cannot wait. At nine-fifty he asks why she is making it into an argument.
details.energy_note: Nothing prevented her. She simply did not get there.

issues.title: Coerced debt
issues.power_abuse_note: Happens between equals too, but is transformed by power
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: The third domain, and the one that outlasts the relationship by a decade: debt taken in her name, with or without her knowledge.

details.aspect: How it is created
details.description: Loans and cards taken out without her knowledge, or signed under threat or manipulation; coercive use of authorised-user status; being made to write a bad cheque or file a fraudulent return.
details.energy_note: Her name, his spending, her credit file.

details.aspect: It does not require overt threat
details.description: It can be produced indirectly - framing the debt as proof of loyalty, or promising repayment with no intention of repaying. A victim may also know coercion is occurring and judge it safer not to challenge it.
details.energy_note: Knowing exactly what it is, and it being safer to sign.

details.aspect: The consequences are structural and long
details.description: 46% of surveyed survivors reported credit damage directly resulting from a partner's actions, and those subjected to coerced debt faced a sixfold higher likelihood of credit denial - impairing housing, loans and jobs with background checks.
details.energy_note: Six times more likely to be refused, for years after he has gone.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the paperwork on the counter
details.description: 'It's just the consolidation thing, saves us about eighty a month.' She signs. It is not a consolidation. She finds out fourteen months later, from a letter, after he has left.
details.energy_note: Signed in four seconds, discovered in fourteen months.

issues.title: The children as the instrument
issues.power_abuse_note: Happens between equals too, but is transformed by power
issues.power_type_note: Acts as or is shielded by an organisation
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists and sometimes works
issues.summary: Contact, schooling and proceedings used to maintain contact and control after separation, through a system obliged to take him seriously.

details.aspect: Proceedings provide lawful, indefinite access
details.description: Applications, variations and appeals require her attendance, her money and her disclosure, and can be renewed for as long as there are children.
details.energy_note: A lawful appointment with him, every few months, for eighteen years.

details.aspect: Handovers are the recurring pressure point
details.description: Regular, mandated, unsupervised contact between two adults, one of whom is afraid, scheduled by an order.
details.energy_note: Ordered to meet him, fortnightly, by a court.

details.aspect: Allegations against her are cheap and effective
details.description: Referrals about her parenting cost him nothing and produce months of assessment for her, as in LEG-002.
details.energy_note: Assessed as a mother, on his say-so.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the Wednesday text
details.description: 'Can we swap this weekend, work thing.' Every fortnight, something small, always requiring a reply, always reasonable. She cannot refuse without it going in a statement, and she cannot stop reading them.
details.energy_note: Reasonable, fortnightly, forever, and she must answer.

issues.title: Wage theft
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable as abuse by a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Unpaid hours, withheld final pay, deductions that were never agreed. The commonest property crime by value, prosecuted least.

details.aspect: The forms
details.description: Off-the-clock work, unpaid overtime, illegal deductions, last cheque withheld pending return of equipment, tips retained, and cash payment with no record.
details.energy_note: Worked, and simply not paid for it.

details.aspect: Recovery costs more than the amount
details.description: Claiming £600 requires a process longer and more expensive than £600, which the employer knows when deciding whether to pay.
details.energy_note: Priced just below the cost of making them pay.

details.aspect: It targets those who cannot complain
details.description: Migrant workers, people on probation, those paid in cash, and anyone whose status depends on the employer, as in IMM-004.
details.energy_note: Aimed precisely at whoever cannot report it.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the final payslip
details.description: 'There was the uniform, and the till was down in July.' Neither was ever raised at the time. It is £340. She has a new job starting Monday and no energy left.
details.energy_note: Three hundred and forty pounds, and she lets it go.

issues.title: The fee that appears at the end
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Knows or controls something about the target
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Disclosed technically, discovered practically, and unavoidable by the time it is visible.

details.aspect: Timing is the mechanism
details.description: Revealed after the switching cost has been incurred - the deposit paid, the documents submitted, the day taken off.
details.energy_note: Disclosed exactly too late to matter.

details.aspect: Technically disclosed
details.description: In the schedule, in the terms, in the clause. The disclosure exists so that the practice is defensible rather than so that anyone knows.
details.energy_note: Written down where it would not be read.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the completion statement
details.description: Four line items she has never seen, totalling £680: file retrieval, electronic transfer administration, archiving, compliance. 'They're standard.' Completion is Thursday.
details.energy_note: Standard, apparently, and due Thursday.

issues.title: Debt collection as harassment
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable as abuse by a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists and sometimes works
issues.summary: Volume, timing and implication used to produce payment regardless of whether the debt is owed.

details.aspect: Contact as pressure
details.description: Frequency, hour, and contact with relatives, neighbours or employers - the social exposure being the actual instrument.
details.energy_note: They call your mother. That is the product.

details.aspect: Implying consequences that do not exist
details.description: Suggestions of arrest, court officers or criminal record where none applies, phrased to survive a compliance review.
details.energy_note: Nothing untrue, and she believes she can be arrested.

details.aspect: Disputed debts continue to be collected
details.description: Sold on, the dispute does not travel with the file, and the process restarts with a new agency and no memory.
details.energy_note: Settled twice, sold three times.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the doorstep visit
details.description: He has a lanyard and a clipboard and stands slightly too close to the door. 'I'm not here to cause trouble.' Her neighbour is in the garden. That is why he came at four on a Saturday.
details.energy_note: Four o'clock Saturday, with the neighbour watching.

issues.title: Family money, taken
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Knows or controls something about the target
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Exploitation by the person with access: the card, the PIN, the power of attorney, the signature on the transfer.

details.aspect: Access is given willingly and early
details.description: Help with banking begins as genuine assistance and does not have a moment at which it becomes something else.
details.energy_note: No day on which it started.

details.aspect: Reporting means accusing your own child
details.description: The victim must name a son or daughter to the police, or to the bank, and most do not.
details.energy_note: The complaint costs her the family.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the helpful son
details.description: 'I'll do the online banking, you shouldn't have to worry about it.' He does. He also moves £400 a month into his own account and calls it his time. When she asks he is wounded, and reminds her who takes her to appointments.
details.energy_note: Wounded that she asked, and she apologises.

details.aspect: Cognitive decline makes it unprosecutable
details.description: Where capacity is in question, consent becomes arguable, and the arguability is frequently the reason the case ends.
details.energy_note: She cannot reliably say she did not agree.

issues.title: Charged more for being poor
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: No mechanism exists
issues.summary: The poverty premium: worse rates, smaller quantities, prepayment meters, and fees that only apply to accounts with no money in them.

details.aspect: The mechanism is automated
details.description: Overdraft fees, late fees, failed-payment charges and higher unit costs apply precisely when there is least money, by design of the product rather than by anyone's decision.
details.energy_note: A charge that only exists when you cannot pay it.

details.aspect: Buying small costs more per unit
details.description: Sachet economics: the smallest quantity has the highest unit price, so the people with least cash pay the most per gram.
details.energy_note: Charged more per gram for having less cash.

details.aspect: There is nobody to appeal to
details.description: The charge is correct under the terms, applied by a system, and the call handler has no authority to reverse it beyond a goodwill limit that runs out.
details.energy_note: Correct, automatic, and nobody's decision.

issues.title: Making it unliveable until you leave
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists and sometimes works
issues.summary: Persistent and deliberate disruption of quiet enjoyment, in order to produce a departure that will be recorded as voluntary.

details.aspect: The recognised tactics
details.description: Cutting utilities, failing to carry out repairs, verbal harassment, repeated entry without notice, and threats of financial injury such as reporting to a credit bureau or refusing a reference.
details.energy_note: Nothing illegal individually. All of it, deliberately.

details.aspect: The motive is usually the rent, not the tenant
details.description: Many cases arise where a landlord wants a lower-paying tenant out in favour of a higher-paying one - so it is economic and not personal, which makes it systematic.
details.energy_note: Not about her. About the difference in rent.

details.aspect: Even a buyout can be coercive
details.description: Offers of payment accompanied by threats or intimidation are prohibited in some jurisdictions precisely because the offer and the pressure arrive together.
details.energy_note: An offer, with the pressure attached.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the inspections
details.description: Monthly, then fortnightly. Always with notice, always exactly 24 hours. He photographs the kitchen each time 'for the file'. Nothing is ever found and he never mentions leaving.
details.energy_note: Entirely lawful, fortnightly, with a camera.

issues.title: The repair that never comes
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Disrepair used as leverage, and the enforcement route built so that using it is riskier than living with the damp.

details.aspect: Reporting risks the tenancy
details.description: In a market with insecure tenure, complaining to the council invites a notice served for unrelated reasons a month later.
details.energy_note: Report the mould, receive a notice in April.

details.aspect: The health cost lands on the household
details.description: Damp, cold and infestation produce respiratory illness in children, which is treated by a health system that does not bill the landlord.
details.energy_note: His damp, her son's chest, the state's bill.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the contractor who is coming
details.description: 'He's booked for Tuesday.' He is booked for Tuesday every week for nine weeks. Each cancellation is somebody else's fault and each is apologised for warmly.
details.energy_note: Nine Tuesdays, nine apologies, one bucket.

issues.title: The deposit
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists and sometimes works
issues.summary: Retained against invented damage, at the exact moment the tenant needs it for the next deposit.

details.aspect: Timing is everything
details.description: Withheld precisely when it is needed for the next tenancy, which forces borrowing and makes disputing it unaffordable in time.
details.energy_note: Held at the one moment she cannot wait.

details.aspect: Fair wear and tear is undefined in practice
details.description: Carpet, paintwork and marks are assessed by the person keeping the money, against a standard nobody agreed at the start.
details.energy_note: Judged by the person who profits from the judgement.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the itemised deductions
details.description: Professional clean £180 - she had it professionally cleaned and has the receipt. Garden £120 - there is no garden. Replacement blind £95 - the blind is in the photographs from move-in, broken.
details.energy_note: Three deductions, two provably false.

issues.title: Refused a home for who you are
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls access to a thing the target needs
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Stated as availability, timing or referencing criteria, never as the actual ground.

details.aspect: The property becomes unavailable
details.description: Available on the phone, taken by the time she arrives, and listed again the following week.
details.energy_note: Gone, and back on the site on Friday.

details.aspect: Referencing criteria do the work
details.description: Guarantor requirements, income multiples, UK-only credit history and no-benefit policies exclude by proxy without naming anything.
details.energy_note: A rule about guarantors that only ever excludes one sort of person.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the viewing
details.description: He is warm on the phone. At the door he looks at her, and at her husband, and says the landlord has just accepted an offer, sorry - he has only just heard. The listing is live for nineteen more days.
details.energy_note: Accepted an offer, nineteen days before it was listed again.

issues.title: The supervisor who owns your degree
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls access to a thing the target needs
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: A structural power imbalance with almost no external check: the person who decides whether years of work becomes a qualification is also the person whose conduct there is no safe way to report.

details.aspect: The measured rate
details.description: A 2018 survey found 24% of doctoral students reported experiencing abuse of power from their supervisors. Another found 21% had experienced bullying, with 48% identifying supervisors as the most frequent perpetrators - and rates of bullying higher in academia than in other workplaces.
details.energy_note: A quarter of them, and the supervisor is usually who did it.

details.aspect: Why nobody leaves
details.description: Once a student is far enough in, the supervisor is so entwined with the project as to be indispensable. Leaving means losing funding, lab access, expertise, the reference and the authorship credit needed for a first postdoc.
details.energy_note: Four years in, and he is load-bearing.

details.aspect: Universities leave it to the individual
details.description: Institutions tend to give supervisors freedom to manage the relationship, which provides few barriers against egregious behaviour and no routine observation of it.
details.energy_note: Nobody else is ever in the room.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the meeting that keeps moving
details.description: Her chapter has been with him eleven weeks. Each fortnight he is about to get to it. In the corridor: 'You're not in a rush, are you? Some people just aren't built for the timeline.' Her funding ends in seven months.
details.energy_note: Eleven weeks, and the delay is now her temperament.

details.aspect: Insecure supervisors bully more
details.description: Research found supervisors in insecure positions significantly more likely to engage in bullying, with productivity demands placing pre-full-professor staff at higher risk - so the pressure on him transfers to her.
details.energy_note: His precarity, discharged downward.

issues.title: Authorship taken
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls access to a thing the target needs
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: The currency of an academic career is allocated by the person with the most to gain from allocating it to themselves.

details.aspect: The supervisor decides
details.description: In most fields supervisors have the power to decide authorship contributions, and at least one first-author paper is frequently required both for the doctorate and for any subsequent post or grant.
details.energy_note: He decides whose name goes first on her work.

details.aspect: The reward system encourages it
details.description: A culture rewarding publication counts, impact factor and authorship rank may encourage faculty to usurp credit - the 'publish or perish' structure rewarding the misconduct it produces.
details.energy_note: The incentive points directly at taking it.

details.aspect: Complaining ends the career it was for
details.description: The person she would complain about writes the reference, sits on the panels, and knows the editors. Being right is not protective.
details.energy_note: Winning the argument ends the reason for having it.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the author order
details.description: 'I've put myself first on this one - it'll travel further with my name on it, which helps you.' She designed it, ran it and wrote it. He is not entirely wrong about it travelling further, and that is what makes it impossible.
details.energy_note: Robbed, with an argument that is partly true.

details.aspect: The catalogue of supervisory misconduct is forty years old
details.description: Goodyear, Crego and Johnston's study had psychologists describe 144 ethically problematic incidents in research supervision, identifying incompetent supervision, supervision abandonment, abusive and exploitative supervision, dual relationships and encouragement to fraud.
details.energy_note: Named and categorised since 1992.

issues.title: The student as free labour
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls money, wages, debt or housing
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Knowledgeable, bright and inexpensive, which the literature names as precisely what makes them targets.

details.aspect: Teaching, marking, admin and his grant applications
details.description: Work outside the research, unpaid or nominally paid, framed as development and impossible to decline.
details.energy_note: Two jobs, one stipend, and the second one is not hers.

details.aspect: Personal errands at the boundary
details.description: Childcare, lifts, house-sitting, moving furniture - the dual relationship the ethics literature names, presented as friendship.
details.energy_note: Collecting his dry cleaning, as a favour.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the summer
details.description: 'I need the dataset cleaned before the September submission. I know you were going home.' She has not been home in two years. The submission is his, with her third on it.
details.energy_note: A third summer, on his paper.

issues.title: Graded by the person you refused
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Formal rank: can instruct, discipline, dismiss
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: The assessment relationship makes any personal advance a coercive one, whether or not it is intended that way.

details.aspect: Consent is structurally unavailable
details.description: Where one party marks the other's work, supervises the project and writes the reference, agreement cannot be distinguished from compliance.
details.energy_note: She cannot say yes meaningfully, so no is not free either.

details.aspect: The mark is the retaliation and is unfalsifiable
details.description: Academic judgement is deliberately not second-guessable, which makes it the perfect instrument.
details.energy_note: A grade, which by design nobody may review.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the withheld results
details.description: Two semesters of results not released, no reason given, four emails unanswered. She had declined an invitation to dinner in October. There is no document connecting those two facts and there never will be.
details.energy_note: Two semesters, and nothing on paper joining them.
details.notes: Structurally identical to the reporter's own account in HAR-001 of assets/text/nigeria.

issues.title: Kept, not developed
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls access to a thing the target needs
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: The opposite instrument: a student valuable enough that finishing is discouraged.

details.aspect: Standards that rise on approach
details.description: Each time the thesis is nearly ready, another chapter is required, another experiment suggested, another reviewer consulted.
details.energy_note: Always one more chapter.

details.aspect: It is indistinguishable from rigour
details.description: Demanding more is what a good supervisor does, which is why this cannot be reported.
details.energy_note: Identical, from outside, to being well supervised.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the fourth revision
details.description: 'It's close. I'd just want to see the longitudinal arm before we submit.' The longitudinal arm is eighteen months. He has a grant renewal in twenty.
details.energy_note: Eighteen months of work, timed to his renewal.

issues.title: Not being believed about your own body
issues.category_name: Medical, clinical and the patient who is not believed
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Holds professional authority over the target's body or mind
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Medical gaslighting: dismissal or minimisation of reported symptoms without adequate justification - distinguished from ordinary dismissal by resting on prejudice and systemic bias.

details.aspect: The documented themes
details.description: A 2024 systematic review identified denial and dismissal of symptoms, delayed diagnosis, negative experiences with staff, gender bias, the need for self-advocacy, stigmatisation of mental health by clinicians, and anxiety and trauma - concluding women's experiences are overwhelmingly negative.
details.energy_note: Seven themes, and the seventh is the trauma of the first six.

details.aspect: The delays are measurable and specific
details.description: Longer diagnostic intervals for multiple sclerosis, optic neuritis, acute coronary syndromes, lupus and chronic pain, with cognitive heuristics disproportionately categorising women's symptoms as functional or anxiety-related.
details.energy_note: Years, per condition, measured.

details.aspect: And the treatment gap is measurable too
details.description: Women attending emergency departments with severe stomach pain waited almost 33% longer than men with the same presentation.
details.energy_note: A third longer, for the same pain.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the fifth appointment
details.description: He has her file open and does not look at it. 'You're quite anxious, aren't you.' She says she is in pain. 'Pain does make people anxious.' He offers an SSRI and a leaflet on sleep hygiene. It is endometriosis, diagnosed four years later.
details.energy_note: Four years, and the first note said anxious.

details.aspect: Being dismissed makes people stop attending
details.description: Patients whose conditions are dismissed may stop seeking care entirely, which produces later presentation, worse outcomes, and a record that appears to show non-compliance.
details.energy_note: She stops going, and that goes in the notes too.

issues.title: The note that follows you
issues.category_name: Medical, clinical and the patient who is not believed
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Knows or controls something about the target
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: A single characterisation entered once - anxious, difficult, drug-seeking, non-compliant - which every subsequent clinician reads before meeting the patient.

details.aspect: It is read before the consultation
details.description: The frame arrives before the patient does, and everything she then says is interpreted through it.
details.energy_note: They had decided before she sat down.

details.aspect: Correcting it is more evidence for it
details.description: Objecting to being described as difficult is straightforwardly confirmatory, which makes the label self-sealing.
details.energy_note: Disputing it proves it.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the handover
details.description: 'She's a bit of a frequent flyer, this one.' Said in the corridor, to the incoming registrar, four feet from the cubicle. She hears it. Neither of them knows she heard it.
details.energy_note: Two words in a corridor, and the next six years.

issues.title: Consent that was not really sought
issues.category_name: Medical, clinical and the patient who is not believed
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Holds professional authority over the target's body or mind
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists and sometimes works
issues.summary: Procedures explained after the decision, alternatives not mentioned, and signatures taken at the point of least capacity to refuse.

details.aspect: Timing removes the choice
details.description: Forms presented in labour, in pain, pre-medicated, or minutes before theatre, when declining is not practically available.
details.energy_note: Signed at the one moment she could not say no.

details.aspect: Alternatives not offered are not refused
details.description: Where only one option is described, the patient's agreement is recorded as a choice between options she was never told about.
details.energy_note: Consented to the only thing she was told existed.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the examination
details.description: 'Just going to have a quick look.' He is already doing it. There are two students at the end of the bed whose presence was not mentioned. Afterwards she cannot decide whether anything happened that she is entitled to be upset about.
details.energy_note: Not sure, afterwards, whether she is allowed to mind.

issues.title: Access as leverage
issues.category_name: Medical, clinical and the patient who is not believed
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls access to a thing the target needs
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: The prescription, the referral, the sick note and the report - each controlled by one clinician and each needed for something outside medicine.

details.aspect: The referral is the only route
details.description: Specialist care, benefits, workplace adjustments and legal claims all require a clinician's signature, which makes disagreeing with him expensive.
details.energy_note: Everything she needs requires his goodwill.

details.aspect: Questioning is recorded
details.description: Seeking a second opinion, querying a dose or bringing research is entered in the notes in language that travels.
details.energy_note: Asking a question, permanently, in the file.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the second opinion
details.description: 'Of course you can. I'll note that you've declined the plan.' He types while saying it. She withdraws the request, and he says that is very sensible.
details.energy_note: One sentence, and she stops asking.

issues.title: Pain, and who is assumed to be exaggerating
issues.category_name: Medical, clinical and the patient who is not believed
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Holds professional authority over the target's body or mind
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: No mechanism exists
issues.summary: Analgesia decisions made on assumptions about the patient rather than the presentation.

details.aspect: The bias runs in both directions
details.description: Some patients are assumed to be exaggerating and are undertreated; others are assumed to be drug-seeking and are undertreated. Both assumptions produce the same outcome.
details.energy_note: Two opposite suspicions, one result.

details.aspect: It is largely unconscious
details.description: Clinicians are described as not deliberately dismissing, but noticing distress and subconsciously reclassifying it - which is what makes it hard to address and impossible to report.
details.energy_note: Nobody meant it, and she is still in pain.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the request
details.description: She asks for something stronger. He says 'let's see how you get on' and does not return. A shift change happens. The note says 'patient requesting opiates'.
details.energy_note: Four words in the file, and nobody comes back.

issues.title: The carer who controls everything
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: The target is in their custody or care and cannot leave
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Dependency for washing, eating, medication and movement, provided by one person, with no witness and no exit.

details.aspect: Withholding is invisible
details.description: Delayed changing, cold food, the call bell moved out of reach, the wait before answering - none of which leaves a mark or appears in any record.
details.energy_note: Twenty minutes longer, every time, and no evidence.

details.aspect: Complaint risks the care
details.description: The person complained about is the person who will be back at eight tomorrow, and everyone involved understands that.
details.energy_note: He is on again in the morning, either way.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the call bell
details.description: She can reach it if she stretches. He puts it on the far chair when he leaves, every time, and says 'there you go' as he does it. If she mentions it he will say he must have knocked it.
details.energy_note: Just out of reach, nightly, deniably.

details.aspect: Isolation is built into the arrangement
details.description: Where care is delivered at home by one person, that person also controls the phone, the visitors and the appointments.
details.energy_note: He is also who decides who visits.

issues.title: Speaking about you, over you
issues.power_abuse_note: Happens between equals too, but is transformed by power
issues.power_type_note: Controls reputation, belonging or standing in a group
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: No mechanism exists
issues.summary: Addressing the companion instead of the person, in the person's presence, about the person.

details.aspect: It removes standing without any statement
details.description: The question goes to the carer, the answer comes from the carer, and the subject of both is sitting between them.
details.energy_note: Discussed, in the third person, while present.

details.aspect: It is done by professionals repeatedly
details.description: Clinicians, officials and shop staff address the accompanying adult by default, which teaches everyone in the room who counts.
details.energy_note: Everyone learns who the real adult is.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the appointment
details.description: 'And does she manage the stairs at home?' She is thirty-four, has a doctorate and is in the chair two feet away. Her sister answers, because not answering makes the appointment longer.
details.energy_note: Her sister answers, because it is faster.

issues.title: Adjustments that are always about to happen
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Acts as or is shielded by an organisation
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: The legally required accommodation, agreed in principle, delayed indefinitely, with the delay attributed to procurement.

details.aspect: Agreement is not implementation
details.description: Nobody refuses. The chair is ordered, the software is being assessed, the room is being looked into, for eleven months.
details.energy_note: Agreed in March, still coming in February.

details.aspect: Chasing becomes the disability
details.description: The person needing the adjustment becomes the person who keeps emailing about it, which is how it is described at review.
details.energy_note: Now known as the one who keeps asking.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the occupational health report
details.description: Recommendations received in April. In November: 'We're waiting on OH to clarify point three.' Point three is a footstool.
details.energy_note: Seven months, for a footstool.

issues.title: Guardianship as capture
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Acts as or is shielded by an organisation
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: A protective mechanism that transfers control of a person's money, home and medical decisions - and whose abuse is, by the accountability body's own finding, of unknown extent.

details.aspect: Nobody knows how big it is
details.description: The GAO concluded the extent of elder abuse by guardians nationally is unknown, citing missing data on how many guardians serve older adults, how many adults are under guardianship, and how many cases of abuse occur.
details.energy_note: Unmeasured, by the body whose job is measuring it.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - what the sampled cases contained
details.description: GAO identified hundreds of allegations of physical abuse, neglect and financial exploitation by guardians across 45 states between 1990 and 2010; in 20 closed cases, guardians stole or improperly obtained $5.4 million from 158 incapacitated victims.
details.money_note: Mean per victim across the 20 closed cases.
details.energy_note: Five point four million, from a hundred and fifty-eight people.

details.aspect: Three quarters of it is financial
details.description: Case analysis found three-fourths concerned financial mismanagement or breach of fiduciary duty - unfiled accounts, improper expenditure, selling property without authority, changing a beneficiary to themselves.
details.energy_note: Mostly not cruelty. Mostly accounting.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the oversight that did not happen
details.description: Courts ignored guardians' criminal and financial problems and failed to review irregular accountings. In one case a $31,000 federal tax lien was filed against a guardian a month after her appointment and she was allowed to continue; in another a social worker served simultaneously as guardian, conservator, representative payee, therapist, landlord and service provider to one victim.
details.energy_note: Six roles, one man, one old woman's money.

details.aspect: The billing is the method
details.description: A prosecutor observed that most financial exploitation by professional guardians occurs through overcharging for services either unnecessary or never performed - lawful-looking invoices rather than theft.
details.energy_note: Invoiced, not stolen.

issues.title: Isolated from the people who would notice
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: The target is in their custody or care and cannot leave
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Visitors discouraged, calls intercepted, and the family member who asks questions gradually excluded.

details.aspect: Isolation precedes everything else
details.description: It is the enabling step: it removes the witnesses, and it is always explained as protecting her from being tired or confused.
details.energy_note: For her own sake, and now nobody visits.

details.aspect: The concerned relative is reframed
details.description: The one asking about the accounts becomes the difficult one, the one who upsets her, the one there is history with.
details.energy_note: The person asking questions becomes the problem.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the phone
details.description: 'She's sleeping.' 'She's just gone down for a nap.' 'She's had a big day.' Four calls, four times. When the daughter finally visits unannounced her mother asks why she stopped ringing.
details.energy_note: Her mother thinks she stopped calling.

details.aspect: The outcomes are severe
details.description: Victims of elder abuse are three times more likely to be at risk of premature death, four times more likely to be admitted to a nursing home, and three times more likely to be hospitalised.
details.energy_note: Three times more likely to die sooner.

issues.title: The will, revised
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Knows or controls something about the target
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists and sometimes works
issues.summary: Pressure applied at the point of dependency, to a document nobody will read until the person who signed it cannot be asked about it.

details.aspect: The evidence is unavailable by design
details.description: Undue influence is contested after the only witness to it has died, which is why it succeeds.
details.energy_note: Disputed after the one witness is gone.

details.aspect: Capacity and pressure are different questions
details.description: She may have capacity and still be under pressure, and the legal test frequently examines only the first.
details.energy_note: Capable of signing, and not free to refuse.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the solicitor's visit
details.description: He arranges it, drives her, sits in the waiting room, and has already told the solicitor she gets confused about money. She signs. He is not in the room, which is the point.
details.energy_note: He waits outside, having spoken first.

issues.title: Neglect that looks like understaffing
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Acts as or is shielded by an organisation
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Care not given, explained by rotas, and indistinguishable from a system under pressure - which it also is.

details.aspect: Both explanations are true at once
details.description: The home is short-staffed and this resident is also left longest. Neither fact refutes the other, and only one is documented.
details.energy_note: Genuinely understaffed, and she is always last.

details.aspect: The evidence is the body

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the visit that was expected
details.description: On the days the family visit she is up, dressed and in the day room. Her son changes his visit to a Tuesday morning without telling anyone, and she is not.

issues.title: Institutions that protected themselves

issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander

issues.summary: The consistent finding across inquiries: the failure was not ignorance. Concerns were raised and the organisation chose its own reputation.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - what the inquiry found
details.description: Institutions frequently did not believe children's disclosures, particularly where the accused denied them; some chose to preserve the alleged perpetrator's reputation and their own above protecting children; concerns were not escalated and information not shared, recorded or acted on.
details.energy_note: They were told. They decided the other way.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - policies existed and were not followed
details.description: Despite significant safeguarding policies being in place, these were not upheld, and inaction or institutional complacency allowed perpetrators to continue undetected. Review recommendations often went unimplemented.
details.energy_note: The policy was fine. Nobody applied it.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - moved on rather than reported
details.description: Institutions reacted to disclosures by moving perpetrators on without investigating or reporting - which transferred the risk to a different set of children and removed the record.
details.energy_note: Transferred, with a clean file.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - disputing that safeguarding applied to them
details.description: Some individuals disputed that they held 'positions of trust' and therefore claimed safeguarding policies did not apply to them - an argument about scope, advanced in place of an answer.
details.energy_note: Arguing about whether the rules covered him.

details.aspect: The structural risk factors are known
details.description: Quality of staff relationships, staffing ratios, establishment size, physical environment, training and openness to external input all affect risk - meaning the conditions are modifiable and were not modified.
details.energy_note: Known, listed, and not acted on.

issues.title: The trusted adult in a closed world
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target

issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Settings involving intense mentorship and extensive one-to-one time, where the adult's professional standing is itself the shield.

details.aspect: Reputation used as cover
details.description: Inquiry findings describe alleged perpetrators harnessing their professional reputations and authority to manipulate other adults and operate undetected.
details.energy_note: The reputation was the method.

details.aspect: Elite sport compared to coercive control
details.description: Abuse dynamics in some sporting contexts have been compared to the coercive control seen in domestic abuse - coaches controlling diet, social activity and relationships, with athletes fearing disclosure would end their careers.
details.energy_note: Controlled totally, with a career as the hostage.

details.aspect: Parental trust reduces oversight
details.description: Ecological analysis of sport identifies excessive parental trust in coaches as itself a risk factor, alongside inadequate supervision and poor club responses.
details.energy_note: The trust was the gap.

details.aspect: Survivor accounts are mostly not the famous cases
details.description: Truth Project work found that unlike the elite cases that attract coverage, survivor accounts reflected far more grassroots contexts - ordinary clubs, ordinary weeks.
details.energy_note: Not the famous ones. The Saturday morning ones.

issues.summary: The disclosure is made and becomes a process problem: handled, minuted, and concluded without the child being told anything.

details.aspect: Framed as consensual or as the child's fault
details.description: Inquiry findings record abuse being framed as consensual and romantic, or blame placed on the child, and conduct characterised by perpetrators as mistakes or poor judgement.
details.energy_note: Reclassified as a mistake, or as her idea.

details.aspect: The child is never updated
details.description: Outcomes are communicated to adults. The person who disclosed learns nothing, and reasonably concludes nothing happened.
details.energy_note: She told them, and then nobody ever mentioned it again.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the reassurance
details.description: 'We've looked into it and it's been dealt with appropriately. You don't need to worry about it any more.' She is fourteen. She is not told what was found, what was decided, or whether he is still coming on Thursdays. He is.
details.energy_note: Dealt with appropriately, and he is there on Thursday.

issues.summary: Where the person exercising power is understood to speak for God, disagreement is not a difference of opinion but a spiritual failure.

details.aspect: The unique facilitation
details.description: Research argues that particular aspects of religion facilitate both institutional and interpersonal manipulation in ways that differ from secular settings - the authority is not merely positional.
details.energy_note: Not his authority. His access to something larger.

details.aspect: Multiple roles at once
details.description: Offenders may occupy several social roles simultaneously - the child's coach and a fellow congregant - which multiplies access and multiplies the cost of disclosure.
details.energy_note: He is three people in her life and all of them matter.

details.aspect: Leaving costs the entire social world
details.description: Community, marriage prospects, family standing, childcare and employment are frequently all inside the congregation.
details.energy_note: The exit costs everyone she knows.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the counselling
details.description: 'Have you prayed about your part in this?' She came to report what her husband does. The conversation is now about her submission, her patience and what she might be withholding. She does not come back.
details.energy_note: Reported him, and left having been assessed herself.

details.aspect: Public accounting creates the obligation
details.description: Where amounts are announced or listed, giving stops being voluntary and becomes a published statement about the household.
details.energy_note: Read out, with the amount.

details.aspect: Prosperity framing makes refusal a lack of faith
details.description: Where giving is linked to blessing, not giving is recast as insufficient belief rather than insufficient money.
details.energy_note: Being broke, reclassified as doubt.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the building fund
details.description: The pledge sheets go round the row. Her neighbour writes £500. The sheet is collected by the man who will read them out on Sunday. She writes £200 and does not eat out in January.
details.energy_note: Two hundred pounds and a thin January.

issues.recourse_note: No mechanism exists
issues.summary: Exclusion administered by a community as a sanction, without any individual doing anything that could be complained of.

details.aspect: Everybody participates and nobody acts
details.description: No one does anything to her. They simply stop - which is not actionable anywhere, by anyone, ever.
details.energy_note: Nothing was done to her. Everything stopped.

details.aspect: It includes the family
details.description: Where the sanction extends to relatives, the cost of maintaining contact is borne by them too, which is how compliance is enforced.
details.energy_note: Her mother is not allowed to phone her.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the announcement
details.description: It is one sentence at the end of the notices, using the formal wording. Nobody looks round. By the Wednesday her sister has stopped replying, and no one has said a word to her.
details.energy_note: One sentence, and a silence that lasts years.

issues.title: The stop that had a reason available
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Can use or threaten force lawfully or otherwise
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: A lawful basis exists, is real, and is not why the stop happened. Pretext is undetectable from inside a single encounter.

details.aspect: The reason is genuine and secondary
details.description: A light, a lane change, a registration check. The ground is sound, and the selection of who to apply it to is not reviewable.
details.energy_note: True, and not the reason.

details.aspect: Compliance does not shorten it
details.description: Being polite, still and cooperative does not reliably end the encounter sooner, which is what the people most stopped already know.
details.energy_note: Doing everything right changes nothing about the length.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the check that keeps going
details.description: Licence, insurance, then the boot, then whether anyone else has driven the car recently, then whose name the finance is in. Twenty-five minutes. No ticket is issued. 'Drive safe now.'
details.energy_note: Twenty-five minutes and no ticket, which is the point.

details.aspect: Objecting is the offence that was available all along
details.description: Obstruction and public order provisions are broad enough that the reaction to a stop can supply the charge the stop did not.
details.energy_note: Nothing to charge, until she objects.

issues.title: In custody, where nobody can see
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: The target is in their custody or care and cannot leave
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable to the target, arguable to a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Control of a person's body, food, medication, sleep and contact with the outside, exercised in a place designed not to be observed.

details.aspect: The deprivations are administrative
details.description: Lights, temperature, the timing of meals, access to a phone call, delay in medication - each defensible as operational and collectively something else.
details.energy_note: Nothing done to him. Several things not done.

details.aspect: The record is written by one party
details.description: Custody logs, timings and accounts of behaviour are produced by the people being complained about.
details.energy_note: His version is the file.

details.aspect: Complaint from custody is structurally weak
details.description: The complainant is in custody, frequently charged, and characterised in the same documents that would be the evidence.
details.energy_note: Complaining from inside, about the people holding the pen.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the blanket
details.description: He asks three times. The third time: 'I'll see what we've got.' Nobody comes. At the handover the incoming officer brings one immediately, and is surprised he did not ask.
details.energy_note: Given instantly by the next shift.

issues.power_type_note: Can use or threaten force lawfully or otherwise
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable as abuse by a bystander
issues.recourse_note: No mechanism exists
issues.summary: The threat is arrest rather than force, applied to people selected because a complaint from them would not be believed.

details.aspect: It is documented as a pattern, not incidents
details.description: Research describes officers intimidating vulnerable citizens with lies and half-truths to obtain sexual activity in exchange for their freedom.
details.energy_note: Freedom, offered as a transaction.

details.aspect: The victims are chosen for irreportability
details.description: Those most targeted are women of colour, LGBTQ+ people, sex workers and anyone vulnerable to threats of incarceration.
details.energy_note: Selected for who will not be believed.

details.aspect: The data barely exists
details.description: Data on sexual assaults by police are almost nonexistent; only a handful of researchers collect it, because departments do not disclose and the research is difficult.
details.energy_note: Almost nobody counts it, so it is almost not there.

details.aspect: Victims are frequently minors
details.description: The national-scale arrest study found victims of police sexual misconduct are typically younger than 18.
details.energy_note: Typically under eighteen.

issues.title: The report that is not taken
issues.power_abuse_note: Cannot happen without a position of power over the target
issues.power_type_note: Controls access to a thing the target needs
issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Discouragement at the counter: no crime number, no record, and therefore no statistic that this happened.

details.aspect: No record means it did not occur
details.description: Crime figures, risk assessments and later prosecutions all rest on the first report having been written down.
details.energy_note: Unrecorded, therefore unhappened.

details.aspect: The discouragement is framed as advice
details.description: 'It's very hard to prove.' 'It'll be your word against his.' 'Do you really want to put yourself through it.' All true, all offered helpfully, all producing the same outcome.
details.energy_note: Talked out of it, kindly, with accurate information.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the front desk
details.description: 'Is he there now? No? Then it's not an emergency.' She has come in person because the line rang out twice. 'Best thing is put it in writing.' There is no crime number and no second appointment.
details.energy_note: Told to write in, and no number given.

issues.summary: The complaint about an institution is assessed by that institution, against standards it sets, on evidence it holds.

details.aspect: They hold all the evidence
details.description: Footage, logs, radio traffic and the officers' own accounts are in the possession of the body being complained about.
details.energy_note: They decide what the evidence was.

details.aspect: Footage is unavailable in predictable ways
details.description: Not activated, not retained, malfunctioning, or overwritten after a retention period that expires during the complaint.
details.energy_note: The camera was off on that one occasion.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the outcome letter
details.description: Nine months. 'The officer's account was found to be credible. No misconduct identified. You may refer the matter to the review body within 28 days.' The review body reviews whether the process was followed. It was.
details.energy_note: Correct process, correct paperwork, nothing found.

details.aspect: The reported volume rose tenfold
details.description: Australia's eSafety scheme recorded reports rising more than 960% from 849 in 2018/19 to 9,060 in 2022/23, led by sexual extortion reports going from 432 to 6,187.
details.energy_note: Four hundred and thirty-two, to six thousand.

details.aspect: The burden of removal falls on the target
details.description: Platforms rely on manual reporting, which is time-consuming and re-traumatising: the person must find and report the material separately on every platform, and cannot pre-emptively report something they cannot prove is there.
details.energy_note: Searching for it yourself, repeatedly, to have it taken down.

details.aspect: Removal is not the end
details.description: Downstream distribution - re-posting by third parties - means each removal addresses one copy, and deplatforming research indicates moderation displaces rather than eliminates.
details.energy_note: Deleted, and already somewhere else.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the message at 2am
details.description: A screenshot of her contacts list. Then: 'I haven't sent it to anyone. Yet.' Then, twenty minutes later: 'I don't want anything. I just want you to talk to me.'
details.energy_note: He does not want money. He wants her to reply.

details.aspect: It is the act of assembly, not of discovery
details.description: Each item may be individually public. Collecting and publishing them together is what creates the harm.
details.energy_note: All of it was findable. None of it was collected.

details.aspect: Platforms treat it as the user's problem
details.description: Analysis of platform risk assessments found technical infrastructure for image removal but, for doxxing and harassment, mitigation centred on educational materials encouraging self-protective practices - responsibility shifted to the target.
details.energy_note: A leaflet about protecting yourself.

details.aspect: Moderation is inconsistent and measurably so
details.description: Analysis reported up to 22% of moderated images as potential false positives, alongside documented cases of moderators intervening on some threads and declining on others.
details.energy_note: Enforced unevenly, and the unevenness is measured.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the helpful thread
details.description: Nobody threatens her. Somebody posts the name of her employer. Somebody else posts the road. A third person posts 'just so people know'. Moderation finds no rule broken in any single post.
details.energy_note: Three posts, no rule broken, and she moves house.

issues.summary: Individually trivial contacts, arriving in volume, from people who will each accurately say they sent one message.

details.aspect: Volume is the weapon and nobody carries it
details.description: Four hundred people sending one message each produces an experience none of them has any idea they participated in.
details.energy_note: Four hundred people, one message each, one target.

details.aspect: Blocking does not scale
details.description: The tools operate per account against a problem that operates per thousand accounts.
details.energy_note: Blocking, for six hours, and still arriving.

details.aspect: It has offline consequences
details.description: Employers contacted, professional bodies notified, reviews left, and family members messaged.
details.energy_note: It reaches her employer by Tuesday.

issues.summary: Mass false reporting used to trigger automated enforcement against the target - the moderation system turned into the weapon.

details.aspect: Automation acts on volume
details.description: Enough reports trigger action before review, so the outcome is produced by coordination rather than by any breach.
details.energy_note: Removed by arithmetic, not by a rule.

details.aspect: Appeal is a form and a wait
details.description: Reinstatement takes weeks if it happens, during which the account, the audience or the income does not exist.
details.energy_note: Restored in five weeks, to a third of the reach.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the coordinated hour
details.description: A group agrees a time. At eight o'clock, ninety accounts report the same three posts. By ten past, the account is suspended pending review. Nobody broke any platform rule.
details.energy_note: Ninety reports in ten minutes, and no rule broken.

issues.summary: An automated determination affecting income, reach or access, with no human decision-maker to name and no reasoning to contest.

details.aspect: No author, no reasons, no appeal that reaches a person
details.description: The decision exists, affects livelihood, and was made by nothing that can be asked why.
details.energy_note: Decided by nobody, and final.

details.aspect: Opacity is defended as anti-gaming
details.description: Explaining the criteria would allow them to be exploited, which is true and also means the affected party can never know what they did.
details.energy_note: A rule that cannot be published, which you must obey.

details.aspect: It falls hardest on people already flagged by geography
details.description: Country-level risk scoring means the same behaviour produces different outcomes depending on where the account connects from.
details.energy_note: Same action, different country, different answer.

issues.visibility_note: Recognisable as abuse by a bystander
issues.recourse_note: A mechanism exists on paper and does not function
issues.summary: Keystrokes, screenshots, location and idle time, disclosed in a policy nobody could decline and still be employed.

details.aspect: Consent is a condition of employment
details.description: Agreement is given at hiring, in a document that cannot be negotiated, by someone who needs the job.
details.energy_note: Consented to, in the sense that refusing meant no job.

details.aspect: The data is used for things it was not collected for
details.description: Gathered for security, produced at a disciplinary, or used to evidence a capability case.
details.energy_note: Collected for one reason, produced for another.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the idle time report
details.description: 'You were inactive 41 minutes on Tuesday.' She was on the phone to a client, on her mobile, because the desk phone was broken and she had reported it twice.
details.energy_note: Forty-one minutes of working, recorded as nothing.

issues.summary: Location sharing, account access and device monitoring, introduced as safety and retained as control.

details.aspect: It extends into every setting
details.description: Stark describes surveillance and behavioural regulation extended into all the settings where the victim previously felt free - which is what distinguishes control from jealousy.
details.energy_note: No room left that is not observed.

details.aspect: Switching it off is the incident
details.description: The monitoring is unremarkable until it stops, at which point the stopping becomes the subject and requires explanation.
details.energy_note: Turning it off is the thing she has to justify.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the concerned text
details.description: 'You've been at your sister's a while x' She has been there fifty minutes. He is not accusing her of anything, and she now knows he is watching the dot.
details.energy_note: One kiss on the end, and she leaves early.

issues.title: Your file, read by people who did not need to

issues.visibility_note: Constructed so that the target cannot prove it happened

issues.summary: Access to records by colleagues, neighbours and relatives working in the institution, undetected unless audited.

details.aspect: Access is broad and logging is passive
details.description: Systems permit wide access for clinical safety, and unlawful access is discoverable only if somebody thinks to look.
details.energy_note: Logged, and nobody reads the log unless asked.

details.aspect: The information travels socially
details.description: The pregnancy, the diagnosis, the termination, the mental health history - repeated at a family gathering rather than published.
details.energy_note: Known at a christening, from a database.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the cousin on reception
details.description: Nobody ever says anything. But her aunt asks, carefully, whether she is 'alright now, after everything'. She has told nobody in the family.
details.energy_note: Her aunt knows, and nobody will ever confirm how.

issues.title: Searched at the border

issues.power_type_note: The target is in their custody or care and cannot leave
issues.visibility_note: Recognisable as abuse by a bystander
issues.recourse_note: No mechanism exists
issues.summary: Devices examined without a warrant under the border exception - messages, photographs, contacts and drafts.

details.aspect: The legal position
details.description: At a port of entry, phones can be searched without a warrant under the border search exception, and the protections that apply elsewhere are sharply reduced.
details.energy_note: Lawful, and total.

details.aspect: Refusing has consequences and complying has none
details.description: Declining to unlock can result in device seizure or refusal of entry; complying provides everything and no protection.
details.energy_note: Two options, and one of them ends the trip.

details.aspect: It reaches other people
details.description: The contents include other people's messages, photographs and contact details - none of whom are present and none of whom consented.
details.energy_note: Her friends' messages, read, in another country.

issues.title: Being told it did not happen
